hook_ideas: A metal that melts in your palm
Liquids that turn solid on impact

key_facts.fact: On a hot pan, water droplets levitate on a vapor layer, skittering without evaporating instantly
key_facts.why_it_matters: It looks like water defies boiling instantly, creating an instant magic-trick vibe anyone can replicate with a kitchen pan

key_facts.fact: Mixing cornstarch and water creates a substance that acts like a solid when hit but flows like a liquid when poured
key_facts.why_it_matters: Viewers love the magic pool feel, turning a kitchen experiment into instant, shareable wonder

key_facts.fact: Gallium is a metal with a melting point of just 29.8°C, so human body heat melts it instantly, turning a solid metal into a liquid blob
key_facts.why_it_matters: It replaces ice melting with metal melting, subverting expectations in a way that feels like a chemistry hack

key_facts.fact: In carbonated soda, raisins sink initially, but CO2 bubbles attach to their wrinkled surface, lifting them up before popping and causing them to fall again
key_facts.why_it_matters: The repetitive rising-and-falling motion feels like a tiny living dance, perfect for keeping eyes on screen

key_facts.fact: Heating a metal ball causes it to expand just enough that it no longer fits through a ring it previously slipped through with ease
key_facts.why_it_matters: It turns a simple geometry problem into a surprising impossible moment that feels rigged but is pure physics
